chapter: Desvigne compared; Piron, Celestin and rivals
title: Walter Barnes and the fatal fire
summary: Barnes's big band burned in a fire; saxophonist Earl Barnes was left behind and survived.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: It wasn't as big as Sidney. He had about 12 pieces. He did a pretty big band. He had about 12 pieces. At that time the big band was on the raise. A lot of big bands like Walter Barnes. Walter Barnes got killed in a fire.
This little saxophone player used to be in his band. At that time. Earl Barnes. He was in the band. Was he killed in this? No, he left. The band left without him.
The other band? No. The other band was from Chicago.

Yeah, Paul. This Barnes, they missed him one night. Somewhere he went out and the band went off without him. Intended to send for him. He was going to meet the band after leaving that. But before he could get to the band, the band would burn out. Yeah, it was terrible.
